chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Working with Billie Holiday again at the Strand Theater, 1951
summary: Basie's band was reorganized for Strand shows where Billie was an act, at a low point in her career.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Did you ever work with her again?

Yes, I worked with her later, with the Count Basie Orchestra, when they started putting stage shows into the Strand Theater in New York City in about 1951. That was the first time that Basie reorganized his big band from his seven-piece band that he had. It was during the time that we went into the Strand Theater, when we had a good band, that was picked up mostly of New York musicians.
And that was about the same time or right before you put the band together that went on the road?
Oh, no. This was the Basie band that I'm speaking of.
Yeah, this was at the time that we started putting that band together, because it was for the express purpose of going into the Strand Theater when Billie was one of the acts.
1951, she was (inaudible). How was her career in 1951?
Not too high. She'd had a few troubles. Health problems.
I remember a concert here in 1948 (inaudible). She was beautiful. She was singing (inaudible).
Well, she had her ups and her downs, which is quite unique with the particular affliction that she had.
